state.brief: Select the concrete reviewer organization to author next for Expense and Creative; source facts and proposed requirements are separated below.
state.task: SEQ-038 concrete expense and image-revision approval protocols; design advice only
observed_source_facts: Expense currently assigns ONE reviewer. submit freezes the claim through existing locks, checks claimant/work membership, a distinct assigned reviewer with current reviewer role and can_work, and matching amount/date ReceiptExtract, then marks submitted/increments submission. decide permits only that assigned reviewer, creates exact immutable Decision evidence before changing status. Rejection requires a reason. Withdrawal is permitted only for a submitted claim whose assigned reviewer is unavailable; correction creates a fresh linked draft preserving history. A corrected claim must obtain its own matching transcription.

Expense reimburse is a SEPARATE finance + current can_work operation, records one full same-currency amount with nonblank unique external payment reference/reason and nonfuture local date, creates Reimbursement before setting reimbursed. It records external payment evidence, not a live payment API. Historical LegacyExpense evidence is not a live approval.

Creative has Template and Revision (not a source model named WorkflowRevision). Owner creative_manager validate freezes exact workflow mapping/file/outputs/duration in Revision, sends validation, then associates its delivery. publish requires that same current owner-manager, active Template, not-yet-published Revision, and exact associated successful valid validation/digest; it sets Revision published/digest BEFORE Template.current. It has NO human request/vote/quorum/expiry/escalation flow. Ordinary members must not receive unpublished graph/validation data through a new review feature.

Task38/plan §4 explicitly require TWO complete ordinary compositions, an eligible distinct two-reviewer quorum case, requester exclusion, duplicate/self/ineligible/stale/revoked refusals, consistent concurrency, exact frozen revision, replay-safe rejection/expiry/escalation, protected review/read operations and separate current-authorized finalization. Quorum/roster/deadline/rejection/escalation below are author POLICY PROPOSALS, not inferred current source defaults.

Every mutation has one authoritative owner. Current selected routing is app + current team with team-root models and inherited child ownership. Package identity/import does not confer record authority or atomic sharing across app/team/D1/DO owners. Current compiler IrStmt::Call refuses canonical cross-operation invocation lowering. Original Expense/Template/Revision models are unexported. Concrete same-owner source compositions/templates are currently authorable; imported mutating extraction requires actual typed exports, same-owner proof and released canonical-call admission/staging. No new approval DSL, universal defaults, separate engine or cross-owner atomic promise is being selected.
common_required_proposed_profile: Use domain-owned typed Request/Vote models and ordinary scenarios, separate immutable common evidence values from domain policies. Freeze exact subject model/ref identity, admitted revision/version/evidence, requester, authorization inputs, reviewer selection and explicit expires input. Expense snapshot binds Expense/submission, submitted immutable fields, amount/currency/receipt and associated matching transcription; Creative snapshot binds exact Revision/parent/definition/file/mapping/outputs/duration and associated validation identity/result digest. Modifying/replacing the subject invalidates existing approval; a new corrected claim/revision never inherits votes. Editing a Template draft must not rewrite approval for a still-identical immutable Revision.

An Expense review's primary remains expense.reviewer and only that primary may create the terminal original Decision with the original by/require checks and write order. Expense requester is expense.parent.user; eligible vote subjects require current reviewer role, active membership/employment and can_work at the frozen location, exclude requester, and retain typed identities. Creative requester is Template.owner; review subjects are current active creative_manager members distinct from requester. Publishing still belongs only to the original owner creative_manager and retains associated validation/active-template/not-published checks and original write order.

Require exactly two distinct effective approvals for these explicit pilots (not a reusable universal default). Expense approval includes its assigned primary plus one independent reviewer; Creative requires two independent nonowner managers. One vote per voter/request; same canonical operation-id replay reuses its receipt, a distinct invocation attempting a duplicate vote refuses. Self/ineligible/foreign-owner/wrong-subject/stale/revoked votes refuse without effects. Protected read grants disclose only the authorized frozen review evidence to requester, permitted finalizer and nominated reviewers, without granting general record/HR/graph access.

At votes AND every final Decision/payment/publication boundary, recheck current reviewer role/work/membership, exact current request/subject/evidence, active source domain, no rejection/expiry/supersession, quorum and current finalizer's own authority. Historical votes/Decisions remain immutable facts rather than role-dependent stored invariants; stored approved status alone is not spending/publishing authority.

The requester supplies an explicit required expires datetime greater than fixed admission now; no default duration or implicit renewal. Any currently eligible authorized reviewer rejection vetoes the request with a required reason. Expiry closes the request without granting authority, erasing historical evidence or manufacturing an Expense Decision. Finalization on or after expiry refuses. Rejection/expiry/escalation use current expected request state/version and canonical operation identity; replay cannot allocate another round or repeated business effects.

Current request-authorized requester can explicitly supersede after secondary loss/expiry or authorized escalation, retaining exactly the same valid immutable subject and original Expense primary or valid Creative owner. Every replacement request resets ALL votes and changes request identity; old request/votes stay immutable and cannot finalize. Loss of the Expense primary BEFORE terminal Decision preserves original submitted withdraw/correct recovery; never silently replace its locked reviewer. Domain rejection remains terminal for that request; Expense primary records original rejected Decision under existing authority, then correction produces a new claim. Creative rejection changes no published/current pointer and can only be reconsidered through an explicitly new request.

Concurrent vote/finalization/supersession attempts use one same-owner fenced transaction with uniqueness and fresh revalidation; outcome is one consistent request/quorum/finalization, no duplicate Decision/payment/publication, no partial vote/business effects on late failure. Quorum approval confers no finance/publication role. Request/Vote operations are exported typed operations with source-owned protected presentation; finalizers cannot bypass their current review gate by an older direct route.

Known residual source-policy uncertainty: original Expense has NO withdrawal/correction transition from approved (only submitted-unavailable withdrawal and rejected/withdrawn correction). Current-review recheck may withhold reimbursement after a post-Decision primary revocation. Do not silently invent an approved-claim reset/reassignment/payment override. This consultation selects the review organization; it does not settle that absent domain recovery policy or qualify its implementation. Full hook/rule/grant and original application runtime qualification remain open.
state.comparison_goal: Choose the least costly explicit review organization for the two same-owner ordinary-source compositions while preserving all listed outcomes. Weigh author/source clarity, reviewer availability, confidentiality, concurrency/recovery complexity and stable future reuse. All options share these constraints; differing selection/order mechanics are not free authority. Package extraction is conditional, not a different alternative approval outcome.

46: ## 4 Reusable approval protocols
47: 
48: **Selected path:** concrete ordinary composition, then a shared package/template where safe. Owners: app/package source, canonical state and identity policies, interfaces/UI. Dependencies: T04/T15/T19/T20, FP.CONTEXT, applicable identity and read-fence tasks, proposal 20. FP.INVOCATION is additionally needed only for approving protected operation values. Witnesses: ExpenseFlow, CanApprove and workbench.
49: 
50: 1. Implement expense review and image revision review with the same outcomes as their explicit current models/scenarios. Separate common evidence values from domain-specific approval/finalization policies. Prove the storage-owner mapping before shared mutating calls; use concrete source templates if an ordinary imported package cannot participate in the same transaction.
51: 2. Identify the exact subject revision and approval requirements. Specify eligible reviewers, distinct votes, exclusion of requester, quorum, rejection policy, expiry, escalation and re-request semantics. Decide each domain policy explicitly rather than hiding it in universal defaults.
52: 3. Export typed request/approve/reject/read operations and protected review presentation. Source ownership derives schemas and actions once. Publishing/spending remains a separate authorized operation that checks current review evidence.
53: 4. Compare all authored models/policies/helpers between concrete duplication, a template and a package. Promote the stable API only if both domains retain their full rules with less source or a clear correctness benefit.
54: 
55: **Acceptance:** two eligible distinct reviewers can reach quorum; duplicate/self/ineligible votes cannot. Concurrent votes have one consistent result; a modified revision invalidates approval; role revocation and stale submission are rechecked; rejection/expiry/escalation are replay-safe. Approved evidence cannot itself grant publication authority.

verified_source_evidence.docs/specification/DESIGN.md:
690: Every mutation has one authoritative storage owner. D1 is the default. A first-class binding can move a whole related group:

705: Each Calendar ID selects one SQLite Durable Object instance; its children inherit it. New root IDs derive deterministically from the complete operation identity, including the originating principal/team/operation, so a fresh replay routes to the same owner. Child references include their root routing identity. The runtime supplies a root-ID/owner directory and authorization context, not a writable D1 duplicate of those records. The directory is an eventual discovery index updated through committed owner work; it never decides record access or availability. A returned root ID routes directly even before indexing completes. Team-scoped browsing of roots uses that directory and loads authorized owner records with bounded fan-out. Cross-owner joins/aggregates are forbidden in business mutations; read views are explicitly eventual. A reference can identify another owner but cannot imply an atomic read or write there. Invariants must live entirely within one owner. Cross-owner workflows use durable events and explicit pending business state. Atomic owner transfers are outside v1.
706: 
707: CRUD and scenarios infer their authority from mutated records and dependencies. A call targeting more than one owner instance fails before commit. Pure shared constants are allowed; mutable remote configuration needed for a decision must be copied into authoritative state with declared version semantics. Admission-time authentication, role, and active-membership facts are a trusted context snapshot, with the revocation boundary in §4; they do not imply a cross-D1/DO transaction. Business eligibility requiring atomic revocation must live at the same owner as the decision. No per-scenario authority selectors, user-written reservation mirrors, or pretend transactions across services.

review_organization.instructions: Which of these three domain-explicit review organizations best supports TWO complete ordinary-source compositions under the verified current sources and required profile? Compare them fairly at identical evidence/authority/failure outcomes. Advice only: do not infer source-missing policies, approval acceptance, runtime readiness or cross-owner/canonical-call support.

criteria.named_roster: Expense uses its existing assigned primary and one explicitly nominated independent currently eligible secondary. Creative uses two explicitly nominated current managers, both distinct from owner/requester. Either can record rejection; approval requires both. Explicit request deadline, current rechecks at terminal Decision/payment/publish and superseding requests with all votes reset apply. Primary loss preserves the existing pending withdraw/correct route. Concrete typed source templates expose domain policy clearly and minimize pool/stage state; unavailable secondary requires explicit replacement rather than opportunistic substitution.
criteria.frozen_pool: Expense freezes a bounded explicitly nominated currently eligible pool containing its mandatory assigned primary; quorum requires primary plus one distinct eligible pool member. Creative freezes a bounded current-manager pool excluding requester and needs two distinct eligible approvals. Any eligible pool member rejection vetoes; deadline/final rechecks/reset-votes/recovery match the common profile. More substitute reviewers can improve availability without stage ordering, but pool size/disclosure/nominations and more possible vetoes require extra explicit policy; no unbounded account/role enumeration.
criteria.staged_concurrence: Expense's assigned primary reviews first, then an explicitly nominated independent eligible secondary concurs; Creative uses a designated nonowner manager first and a different nonowner manager for concurrence. Either eligible nominated reviewer can veto the request; the second affirmative stage requires completion of the first. Both approvals/current checks remain required before separate original finalizers. Deadlines/supersession/reset-votes/recovery are unchanged. Clear sequential responsibility can help auditability, but phase state, unavailable-stage recovery and concurrent-arrival refusals add complexity/latency.
